key_insight: A regularized flow approaching a proposed Navier–Stokes singularity can trigger magnetic reconnection that splits a flux ring into daughter rings.
engineering_relevance: The results connect rapidly collapsing flow structures to magnetic topology changes, informing the modeling of strongly driven conducting fluids and plasmas.
method: Simulate a magnetic ring with resistive magnetohydrodynamics under an imposed, regularized collapsing flow.
Remove the imposed drive at the nominal singular time and track subsequent reconnection.
Analyze poloidal-flux bifurcations and Lorentz feedback, with three-dimensional simulations checking persistence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter-free cusp predictions of daughter-ring asymmetry for single-island splits, while three-dimensional simulations retain splitting and merger.
watch_item: The imposed flow is regularized, so these simulations do not establish a Navier–Stokes singularity or its consequences in an unregularized physical system.
paper_title: Magnetic flux ring splitting near a Navier-Stokes singularity
